samples.summary: Any click inside a preview task item toggles it — including the mouseup that ends a text-selection drag or a double-click
samples.evidence: `onTaskClick` is bound to `click` on the preview root and toggles whenever `target.closest('.task-list-item')` matches, filtering only `a, button`. A `click` event still fires after a drag that selects text inside the item (and twice for a double-click word-select), so simply selecting/copying the text of a task rewrites the source line (`setTaskChecked` -> `view.dispatch`), i.e. an unintended document mutation that also propagates to peers via `noteSync`. Nothing checks `window.getSelection()?.isCollapsed`, `e.detail`, or a mousedown/mouseup position delta.

samples.summary: `Number.isInteger(Number(null))` is true — a task item missing `data-source-line` silently toggles document line 1
samples.evidence: `const line = Number(item.getAttribute(TASK_LINE_ATTR)); if (!Number.isInteger(line)) return;` — `getAttribute` returns `null` when the attribute is absent, and `Number(null) === 0` (also `Number('') === 0`), which passes the integer guard. The click then calls `onToggleTask(0, ...)` -> `setTaskChecked(view, 1, ...)`, flipping whatever checkbox happens to be on the first line of the note instead of the clicked one. The guard should test the raw string (e.g. `attr === null` / `/^\d+$/`) before converting.

samples.summary: Task items the preview renders as clickable are silently non-toggleable when the source line does not match LIST_RE (e.g. inside a blockquote)
samples.evidence: `LIST_RE = /^(\s*)([-*+]|\d{1,9}[.)])(\s+)(?:\[([ xX])\]\s)?([\s\S]*)$/` only matches a marker at the start of the line, so `> - [ ] a` parses with `marker: ''` and `check: null`, and `setTaskChecked` returns at `if (p.check === null) return;`. markdown-it, however, renders that item with an enabled `.task-list-item-checkbox` and the new `cursor: pointer`, and `onTaskClick` calls `e.preventDefault()` — so the user clicks, the box visibly reverts, and nothing at all happens with no feedback.

samples.summary: Clicking a plain nested list item inside a task item toggles the ancestor task instead
samples.evidence: `target.closest(`.${TASK_ITEM_CLASS}`)` walks *up* the tree, so for markup like `- [ ] parent` with a nested plain `- child`, a click on `child`'s text finds no class on its own `<li>` and resolves to the parent task `<li>`; `item.querySelector(TASK_CHECKBOX_SELECTOR)` then returns the parent's checkbox and the parent's `data-source-line` is flipped. The CSS also paints the whole nested region `cursor: pointer`, so this looks intentional to the user.

samples.summary: With multiple cursors the checkbox input handler drops the typed space at every non-main range
samples.evidence: The handler inspects only the main range (`from`/`to` args) and dispatches a single change for `line.from..to`, then returns `true`, which suppresses CodeMirror's default insertion for *all* ranges. If the user has several cursors and the main one sits after a bare `[ ]`, the other cursors receive no space at all — typed input is silently lost. The same handler also does not use the passed `insert` fallback for the other ranges.

samples.summary: Toggling a task list to bullets/ordered discards the checked state irrecoverably
samples.evidence: `toggleKind` builds the new prefix with `check: kind === 'task' ? (p.check ?? ' ') : null`, and the ordered branch with `check: null`. So `- [x] a` -> Bullet gives `- a`; toggling Checkbox back yields `- [ ] a`, i.e. the `x` is gone. Since the two toolbar toggles are adjacent and one click apart, a mis-click silently loses the completed state of every selected task (the intermediate state is only recoverable via undo).

samples.summary: Turning a list off keeps the leading indent, which can turn a nested item into an indented code block
samples.evidence: In `toggleKind`, the off-toggle path is `if (all) return p.indent;` — the marker is stripped but the whitespace is kept. A nested item like `      - a` (6 spaces, two levels of ordered nesting) becomes `      a`, which markdown then renders as an indented code block rather than a paragraph. The plain-text conversion should normally drop the indent (or clamp it below 4).

samples.summary: List state re-parses every selected line on every selection change — O(doc) work while drag-selecting a large note
samples.evidence: `computeActiveFormats` now calls `computeListState`, which calls `selectedLines` and runs `LIST_RE` over *every* line in the selection. The editor's `updateListener` fires it on each `selectionSet`/`docChanged`, so dragging a selection (or Cmd-A then typing) across a multi-thousand-line note re-parses the whole range on every event. The previous inline-format computation was O(1) slices. Only the first/last few lines plus a bounded scan are actually needed for `kind`/`canIndent`.

samples.summary: The five new list commands are exposed on NoteEditorAPI with no read-only guard, unlike the preview toggle
samples.evidence: `onToggleTask` is explicitly `readOnly ? undefined : ...` (editor.ts:230), but `toggleBulletList/toggleOrderedList/toggleTaskList/indentList/outdentList` call into `view.dispatch` unconditionally. `EditorView.editable.of(false)` blocks user input, not programmatic dispatch, so any host calling these on a read-only share mount would mutate the doc and push it through `noteSync`. Today only `notes-toolbar.tsx` calls them and it hides the group behind `canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== 'view'`, so this is currently unreachable — but the guard lives only in the UI.

samples.summary: Ticking a task re-renders the whole preview via innerHTML, which can jump the preview's scroll position and re-run mermaid
samples.evidence: `onTaskClick` deliberately does not update the DOM; the resulting `docChanged` triggers `renderPreview()` -> `this.el.innerHTML = md.render(...)`. Replacing the whole subtree drops image/mermaid layout momentarily, so the scroll container (and the editor pane, via the scroll-sync listeners installed in editor.ts) can jump away from the item the user just clicked. Typing already did this, but it previously happened in the *editor* pane; now it is triggered by a click in the pane whose scroll position is being disturbed.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described. `preview.ts:234` binds `onTaskClick` to `click` on the preview root for any non-read-only mount (`editor.ts:228-233`). `onTaskClick` (preview.ts:246-266) toggles whenever `target.closest('.task-list-item')` matches, filtering only `a, button` (line 251), and calls `onToggleTask`, which reaches `setTaskChecked` -> `view.dispatch` (editor.ts:232, list-commands.ts:283-295) — a real document edit that syncs. There is no check of `window.getSelection()?.isCollapsed`, `e.detail`, or a mousedown/mouseup delta anywhere in preview.ts, and no CSS guard either: notes-preview.css:346-349 only sets `cursor: pointer` (no `user-select: none`), so item text is selectable and a drag-select or double-click ending inside the `<li>` fires `click` on it. This is an unintended state mutation on a real user path (select-to-copy), squarely in the correctness lane.

verdict.reason: The cited code exists verbatim at packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:253-254 and the guard is genuinely ineffective for a missing attribute: getAttribute returns null when data-source-line is absent, Number(null) === 0, and Number.isInteger(0) is true, so the guard passes and onToggleTask(0, ...) fires (preview.ts:265). That reaches editor.ts:232 (setTaskChecked(view, line + 1, ...)) and list-commands.ts:278-296, whose own bounds check (:283) does not reject line 1; only the p.check === null test (:286) limits damage, so a stray click would flip whatever checkbox sits on the note's first line — wrong-line content mutation. I could not refute reachability from the repository: the attribute is only guaranteed by the local core rule at preview.ts:58-68, whose precondition (markdown-it always populating list_item_open.map, and markdown-it-task-lists only ever attaching 'task-list-item' to a list_item_open token) depends on library internals that are not inspectable here — node_modules is absent, with the dependency only pinned in packages/notes/package.json:66 and pnpm-lock.yaml:7599. Local plugins (details-plugin.ts:46-96, list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:181-199) do not synthesize list items, which makes the bad path unlikely, but "unlikely based on unread library source" is not a citable refutation ground, and the defect is a real logic error in the guard's condition regardless. Confirmed with low confidence on reachability; impact if it fires is document corruption.
